rv.q: All four of these capable performers are ensemble players and keen listeners, expertly wearing their characters on their sleeves, and providing engagingly organic performances.
While Machine Learning is not nearly as fascinating as that unsettling little play, it does give me a clear sense of the stories that make Little Engine chug.
Machine Learning is a tight 90-minute drama with a stellar cast that explores companionship and the human condition (as all good sci-fi should).

Under the wonderful direction of Irish-born director Colm Summers , the show blends humor and seriousness, dealing with topics like emotionally abusive relationships, sociopathy, and infant death, while exploring artificial companionship.

While the play generates the suspense and menace of a thriller, it also proves effective if viewed purely as a domestic tale, as the verbal sparring, kinder interactions and shifting allegiances reveal four compelling characters.
Australian playwright Kate Vozella's Machine Learning is one of the most pleasant surprises of the fall season.

cn.t: Fiercely acted drama about relationships unraveling in confinement largely succeeds, though critics find the AI premise underwhelms its marketing promise. Strong performances elevate intimate character work over technological themes.

vr.q: a piece that has a cool premise, but ultimately lacks clarity
